newsitem.title: FINLAND: Analysts upbeat on Konecranes report. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Analysts upbeat on Konecranes report. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]

text.p: Equities analysts on Wednesday were upbeat on Finnish cranes maker KCI Konecranes International Oy after the company's 1996 earnings had topped expectations.
"This was an extremely good report," said Pontus Gronlund, analyst at Aros Securities (corrects brokerage name from ABB Aros Securities).
"Margins were better in all business groups."
Konecranes reported a 54 percent rise in 1996 profit after financial items to 208.2 million markka, above the highest forecast of 200 million markka in a Reuters poll.
"Even though I upped my forecasts in the autumn all divisions have now performed better than I expected -- above all maintenance has risen fast," said Jussi Hyoty of AG Private Bankers.

The maintenance services business area's 1996 sales were 1.16 billion markka, up 29 percent on 1995. The standard lifting business area's sales rose 13 percent year-on-year to 905.7 million markka, but the special cranes' sales fell 11 percent to 609.4 million markka.
"They were still rather cautious after the second tertial," Hyoty said. "So this excellent result may even have surprised the company a bit."
"Of course this is their most important tertial," said Carnegie analyst Roar Nilsen referring to September-December.
"They usually say they will make no profit in the first tertial, one-third of their profit in the second and two-thirds in the last tertial -- that's the company's rule of thumb," Nilsen said.
"They appear very positive about the outlook," he said.
With the share up almost 10 percent, at 178.00 markka, Nilsen said the stock could be trading at a slight premium.
"That could be even a bit more bullish than the report," he said, but added: "At these levels it is fairly well priced."
